Yet when the water breaks, it is loud and deep, A roar that shakes the foundations of the ship. The waves do not speak with words or tongues of gold, But carry thoughts of days that have passed away. They trace a path where shadows meet the light again, Or crash against the cliffs to show their shape. Some say they are gods who watched and kept it quiet, Others whisper they have loved the ocean too. A sailor waves his hat in waves he cannot see, As if he knows the sea will never go away. He holds a lantern, a torch burning bright within, To find the path to land or reach the shore again. The tide rises slowly until it meets the moon, And then, with sudden force, it pulls back and turns. It is not cold nor hot, but feels like stillness deep, Where stars are scattered in a space of deep blue light. No wind blows through the waves that touch the sea's crest, Only the rhythm of time moving along its side. The ocean knows no names, no stories or words, Just vast, endless black and white in quiet days. Sometimes it whispers secrets from the depths below, That the world is made of water and a thousand drops. We drown in the silence until we wake again, As waves come flooding back to make space for us once more. But even then, we know the sea will return again, And bring the same quiet, calm, and endless light above. So let the tide be slow, let the wind stop blowing, And listen closely to what lies beneath the water's floor. It is not always loud or violent in its flow, But it is also gentle, a song of vast and deep. A promise that if we ever walk on land again, The sea will wait for us until we have been there all long enough.
